query: A Guest Who Wants More {A guest with rings on every finger has been generous all night, and now pushes a heavy purse across the table. "Come back to my inn," he says. "Just to talk." The house rule is clear.|Another guest, another heavy purse, another invitation "just to talk". The landlady is busy across the room.|You know the look now: the generous hour, then the purse, then the invitation. Tonight it comes from a woman in pearls.} Call the landlady {The landlady has the guest down the stair in a minute, purse and all. You're paid for the hours, and shaky for the rest of the night.|"The stair," says the landlady, and the guest takes it. You keep your wage and lose the tip, and your hands won't stop shaking.|The guest is shown out. The landlady pours you something strong and pays you for the night. It doesn't feel like enough.} Keep the purse, promise nothing {You let him believe tomorrow, and then the day after. He leaves the purse. You feel like a pickpocket with good manners.|You laugh, and keep the purse, and see the guest into a carriage, alone. It's the most you've earned in a night. You don't sleep.|You promise nothing in a way that sounds like something. She leaves happy and you leave rich, and a little ashamed.} {He sees through you, and takes his purse back with a hand that grips too hard. The landlady throws him out, too late.|The guest makes a scene on the stair, loudly calling you a cheat. A prefect on the stair hears every word.|She wants the purse back, loudly, and the landlady gives it to her. You go home with nothing but a bruise on your wrist.}
